text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Tax reform plans presented by the government yesterday include cuts in income tax amounting to 75 billion francs over a five-year period, to increase workers' purchasing power. Change in tax rates meant to help low-income families and the most heavily burdened taxpayers. Payroll social security contribution is to go down 1.3 percent to help employment, while general social contribution (CSG) is raised and extended to savings. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- First half results released this month by major French groups show sustained growth in spite of a difficult economic situation, thanks to their international activity.
-- Credit du Nord returns to profit in the first half.
-- Germany posts a 1.5 percent increase in GDP for the second quarter, remains burdened by a 10.2 percent unemployment rate.
-- Credit Lyonnais workers worried over government reshuffling of the ailing bank's bailout plan, while Senate members wish the Finance Ministry would put the bank up for sale.
-- Retail sector posts rise of activity in August.
-- Bouygues sells U.S. subsidiary for some 280 million francs.
-- Industry Ministry wants the state to pull out gradually from the nuclear industry.
-- The Bank of France intervened to back the franc against the mark yesterday after Germany posted Q2 GDP growth up 1.5 percent.
